chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abi Jamilah, from al-Halabi, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted:
"Then whoever transgresses after that, for him is a painful punishment."
He said: "It is the man who pardons or takes the blood money, then wounds his companion or kills him; for him is a painful punishment."

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation paid in lieu of retaliation
key_terms.الْعَفْوُ: pardon of the offender by the injured party or guardian
key_terms.عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ: a painful punishment for unlawful retaliation
key_terms.يَجْرَحُ: inflicts a wound or bodily injury

ai.seo_question: Who is meant by 'whoever transgresses after that' in this Qur'anic verse?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic phrase as referring to a person who, after granting pardon or accepting blood money, later assaults or kills the offender. It emphasizes the binding nature of legal settlement and condemns any further retaliation as a punishable transgression.
